issues.failure_explanation: CP0 consists of one point, and every nonempty design set there is a singleton. The infimum defining D_t is therefore over the empty set; it is undefined as a finite distance, or +∞ under the extended-real convention. It cannot be comparable to 1/t.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict this proposition to n≥1 and handle the S1 case of the main theorem directly.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition cannot be used in the n=0 case included in the main proof.
issues.title: The nearest-neighbor proposition is undefined on CP0
issues.why_classification: A trivial one-point/one-circle base case removes the defect without excluding any intended positive-dimensional sphere result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: eigenfunctions of $\Delta_{\Bbb{CP}^n}$ in $L^1(\Bbb{CP}^n)$ of eigenvalue at most $4t(t+n)$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed local formula is the div-grad Laplacian, whose nonconstant spherical eigenvalues have negative sign. The proof subsequently treats the same operator as having positive eigenvalues i(i+2n). With the displayed sign, an upper cutoff at the positive number 4t(t+n) does not restrict to low degrees; it includes arbitrarily negative eigenvalues. The spectral implication used to identify R_t with P_t is therefore invalid under the operator actually calculated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the nonnegative Laplacian −div-grad consistently and insert the corresponding minus signs in the local calculations, or change every spectral cutoff consistently for the opposite convention.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of the diffusion-polynomial space and the proof of its equality with the finite-degree polynomial space use incompatible conventions.
issues.title: The Laplacian sign is incompatible with the spectral cutoff
issues.why_classification: A consistent local sign convention restores the intended spaces and thresholds without changing the construction or any asymptotic rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Combining these facts with two applications of \eqref{eq:MDelta}

issues.failure_explanation: The prescribed pullback coordinates are fiber-adapted coordinates, not generally geodesic normal coordinates on the total sphere. Already near (1,0) in S3, if (u,v,w) are spherical normal coordinates with u vertical, the projective affine coordinate z2/z1 has expansion v+uw+i(w−uv)+higher-order terms. Its real and imaginary pullbacks therefore have nonzero quadratic terms and cannot be normal-coordinate functions. The Laplacian intertwining identity does not follow from the assumed chart.

failure_location.quote: Setting $x_i:=\Pi^*x_i^{\Bbb C}$, we may then consider geodesic normal coordinates $\{x_i:S^{2n+1}\to\Bbb R\}_{i=1}^{2n+1}$ on $S^{2n+1}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove Laplacian intertwining using the Riemannian-submersion structure and the geodesic circle fibers, with smooth test functions, instead of the nonexistent simultaneous normal coordinates.
issues.overall_effect: The nontrivial identification of algebraic and diffusion polynomial spaces lacks a valid proof at its Laplacian step.
issues.title: Pullbacks of projective coordinates cannot be assumed to be spherical normal coordinates
issues.why_classification: A contained differential-geometric lemma can establish the intended identity, but the coordinate argument must be replaced rather than locally reindexed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we take $X_0$ to be the union of the vertices of a regular $(t+1)$-gon on each element of $Y_{y_0}:=Y\setminus\{y_0\}$

issues.failure_explanation: For d=2n+1, the projective design has order t^(2n)=t^(d−1) fibers. The proposed point set places t+1 distinct points on every fiber except one, so |X0|=(t+1)(|Y|−1), of order t^d for n≥1. The cited construction does not establish the advertised t^(d−1) point count.

failure_location.quote: whose constituent point sets and curves have asymptotic orders of size and length $t^{d-1}$ and $1$ respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the point-set rate by t^d. Retaining t^(d−1) would require a different construction or an additional substantial argument.
issues.overall_effect: The hybrid construction's advertised point complexity is understated by a factor of order t.
issues.title: The hybrid point-set complexity omits one factor of t
issues.why_classification: The source-supported correction materially worsens the expressly advertised complexity exponent.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a plane $P\subset\Bbb{R}^{d+1}$ which intersects $S^d$ in a circle

issues.failure_explanation: Replacing a circle of length a transfers mass (1−ρ)a/ℓ(γ), not 2π/ℓ(γ). The circle need not have length 2π, and merging its polygon with X also requires equal per-point weights. As a direct counterexample, combine an antipodal 1-design set with a great-circle 1-design using ρ=1/2. Taking that whole circle as the removable part gives the proposed new balancing constant 3/2, outside [0,1].

failure_location.quote: $(X,\gamma,\rho)$ is a hybrid $t$-design if and only if $(X\cup X_P,\gamma_P,\rho+2\pi/\ell(\gamma))$ is a hybrid $t$-design.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use ρ'=ρ+(1−ρ)a/ℓ(γ), require disjoint point sets and the compatibility ρ/|X|=(1−ρ)a/(ℓ(γ)|X_P|) for an unweighted union, and specify the arc-length decomposition and zero-mass cases.
issues.overall_effect: The stated general hybrid equivalence and its justification of subsequent replacements are invalid.
issues.title: The hybrid replacement rule does not preserve component masses
issues.why_classification: A corrected balanced replacement lemma retains the polygon-circle strategy, but the unrestricted rule needs substantive additional conditions and corrected normalization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a smooth manifold $M$ and a subspace $P\subset L^1(M)$

issues.failure_explanation: An L1(M) equivalence class has no well-defined restriction to a lower-dimensional submanifold or pointwise supremum. For example, when N has ambient measure zero, the zero function and 1_N represent the same L1(M) element but have different integrals over N. Ambient integrability also does not ensure integrability of a chosen representative on N. Thus the property is not defined for the announced general class of subspaces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict P to actual continuous or smooth functions on M, as in the polynomial examples, or supply a specified trace operator and hypotheses ensuring the required integrals exist.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed general P-design submanifold notion is ill-defined beyond function spaces with specified traces.
issues.title: The submanifold definition uses traces and suprema of arbitrary L1 classes
issues.why_classification: The polynomial examples survive, but the stated arbitrary-L1 generality must be restricted or replaced by a nontrivial trace framework.
